newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ross faces legal action in Solomon Islands.
newsitem.headline: Ross faces legal action in Solomon Islands.

text.p: More than 1,200 landowners have started legal action against Ross Mining NL over its proposed A$61.1 million gold mine in the Solomon Islands, Melbourne law firm Slater and Gordon said on Monday.
The landowners were named in two proceedings lodged in the Solomon Islands High Court, the law firm said in a statement.
The first case involves 215 landowners from the Gold Ridge mining lease area who are asking that a compensation agreement made by Ross in obtaining its mining lease be declared void.

The second writ was lodged on behalf of 1,024 landowners from an area next to the Matepono River and its tributaries who want development of the mine restrained because they believe it will cause "severe environmental damage" to the river.

Slater and Gordon last year won a compensation package for villagers in Papua New Guinea who had lodged environmental claims against The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd over the discharge of mine tailings from the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine into the Fly River system.
Ross shares were down one cent at 67 cents at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
